PTU treatment of young rats results in a decreased responsiveness of the kidney and of the hypothalamoneurohypophyseial system to salt load, which is probably due to the lack of T3 during the development of the animal.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PTU-treated young rats are unable to concentrate urine at the age of 35 days, and the ability to concentrate urine does not appear until the age of 50 days.
the PTU-treated young rats have a decreased capacity to excrete salt load, which may be related to a decreased AVP release by the neurohypophyses and to an altered response of the kidney to AVP.

the PTU-treated rats are unable to compensate the osmotic load in normal delays because they are unable to respond to the osmotic load with a rapid increase of the plasma AVP level and with the subsequent rapid increase of the AVP concentration in the urine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PTU-treated rats have an abnormal response to salt load, with an altered AVP release and a delayed recovery of the natremia.
PTU treatment of young rats leads to an impairment of the kidney's response to salt load, and this may explain the high natremia of the PTU rats.
